questions.prompt: You compute np.var(x) on a sample of 5 values. Compared with the unbiased sample variance, the result is:
options: 20% too small (it divides by n instead of n − 1)
questions.explanation: NumPy's default ddof=0 divides by n = 5 instead of n − 1 = 4, so the result is 4/5 of the unbiased estimate. Pass ddof=1.

questions.prompt: You collect 4× as many users. What happens to the standard error of the mean?
questions.explanation: SE = s/√n, and √4 = 2. Precision grows with the square root of the sample size.

questions.prompt: A bootstrap function returns the same interval width of exactly 0 for every dataset. The likeliest bug is:
options: One resample was reused for every replicate, so all replicates are identical
questions.explanation: If every row of the index matrix is the same draw, every replicate is the same number and the percentiles coincide. Each replicate needs its own resample.

questions.prompt: What does a correctly working 95% confidence interval procedure guarantee?
options: The true value has a 95% chance of being in this particular interval after it's computed
95% of the data fall inside the interval
About 95% of intervals built from repeated samples contain the true value
The estimate is within 5% of the truth
questions.explanation: Confidence is a property of the procedure over repeated sampling, which is exactly what a coverage simulation measures.
